about.title: City of Industry Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: City of Industry is a working city, and most people pass through it rather than live in it. Trucks move between warehouses along Valley Boulevard and Gale Avenue, commuters cut across on Azusa Avenue and Hacienda Boulevard, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. are when public records show collisions clustering. In 2025, the city logged 207 injury collisions, 282 people hurt, and 3 traffic deaths. Behind each of those three deaths is a family trying to sort out what happens next. A wrongful death claim under California law is one way a family can hold a negligent driver, employer, or property owner accountable in civil court, apart from anything prosecutors may or may not do. The claim can cover funeral and burial costs, the income your loved one would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of love, companionship, and guidance. LawProactive does not handle cases ourselves. We simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who does, and who works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in City of Industry Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can tell you plainly whether you qualify.

items.title: Deadlines you may not know about
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but that window shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. Getting connected early protects your family's ability to act.

items.title: No cost to you, at any stage
items.desc: Our connection service is free, and the independent attorneys we work with take wrongful death cases on contingency. If there is no recovery, there is no attorney fee.

items.question: My family member was killed in a truck collision on Gale Avenue while working. Can we still bring a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Possibly, though it depends on who was at fault. If the death happened on the job, workers' compensation death benefits may apply, and those rules limit claims against the employer. A separate wrongful death claim may still be available against a third party, such as another driver or a trucking company, and an attorney can sort out which path fits your situation.

items.question: The other driver is being charged criminally. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs independently of any criminal prosecution. The two cases have different standards of proof and different goals, so a conviction is not required for your civil claim to succeed, and waiting could risk the two-year deadline.

items.question: What can our family actually recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: Recoverable losses generally include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have contributed over their lifetime, and the loss of their love, companionship, comfort, and guidance. Every family's circumstances are different, so no one can promise a particular result. An attorney can walk you through what applies to your situation.
